task: Extend sort-key ordering-law tests to named key functions imported from another module (S3.2).
observation: An untyped key imported from another module and used only as `sort(v, by: keys.loose)` passed `moss check` and Fast Debug, but the native build failed in rustc with `cannot find function __moss_specialize_keys__loose_0`. The same key worked when the consumer also called `keys.loose(3)` directly: module projection collected consumer-side specialization edges for direct calls and pipeline stages, but not for sort keys.
impact: The L7 source-free sort test used a typed key inside the provider, so the cross-crate untyped-key path had never been exercised. Any package exporting a generic key helper would have hit a backend failure after a clean check.

resolution.summary: collect_local_call_sites now records the sort key as a call edge at the element type, like a pipeline stage; same-package, path-dependency, and compiled-only provider regressions pass in all engines.

reproducer: module keys: export fn loose(x): return x; module app: var ints = [3, 1, 2]; sort(ints, by: keys.loose); echo ints[0]

task: Make Map/Set key-protocol fixtures that are fail-closed until MossMap<K,V> exists (S3.3).
observation: Only Float keys fail closed today. A Map keyed by any record or nominal type passes `moss check` whether its isequal/hash proof is valid, malformed, impure, partial, or missing; native rustc then rejects the HashMap (`Name: Eq` not satisfied) and Fast Debug compares keys structurally, ignoring the custom methods (wrong lookups or `missing map key`). Empty `Map()` uses not pinned at construction (never-inserted get, `Map().get`, open-result helper, unused Map) likewise pass check and fail in rustc.
impact: The task assumed the fixtures would all be rejected before native execution; 19 of 30 cannot be, so the runner records them as known-failing with the observed rustc error instead of claiming fail-closed. The record-key gap also means Fast Debug silently gives different answers than the intended key protocol.

resolution.summary: Handed off: record-key admission to the MossMap<K,V>/KeyProof work, unpinned empty Maps to Team G Option B. Not fixed locally per S3 scope.

task: Assert that an impure key imported from another module is rejected by the checker (S3.2).
observation: `moss check <project-directory> --json` returned `ok: true` with an empty diagnostics list for a project whose main module uses a printing sort key; `moss check src/main.moss --json`, `margo build`, and `margo debug` in the same project all reported SORT_KEY_IMPURE.
impact: A directory argument looks like a successful project check but checks nothing, so a test or agent that passes the project path gets a false pass. The first draft of the S3 test did exactly that and only the expected-failure assertion exposed it.

resolution.summary: The suite checks the entry file and also requires margo build and margo debug to reject; the directory behaviour is recorded as P25-S3-L4 for the tooling owner.

suggestion: Reject a directory argument with a structured error, or check the project's entry module.
